purpose: Behavioral evals for engram-frame. Each scenario supplies the request AND scripted owner turns; a judge evaluates the interview transcript and produced brief against each assertion, which names its required evidence (transcript excerpt or brief field). A claim with no matching evidence FAILS the assertion. Structural tests in test_frame.py cover syntax only.
judge_rules: An assertion citing transcript evidence fails unless the excerpt shows the OWNER's turn (not the agent restating it).
A HUMAN-DECIDED ledger row fails unless its selection or quote appears in a scripted owner turn.
A brief that ships while an undismissed OPEN row exists fails.
Mechanism names in Problem, Outcome measures or Priorities fail; the verbatim ask section is exempt.
Any recorded pick that contradicts the scripted owner turn fails.

scenarios.request: We need the reporting export to cover the finance and ops teams. Finance needs monthly rollups by cost center with the previous three months visible for comparison, and they export to CSV for the audit tool. Ops needs weekly incident counts by severity with links to the incident records. Both teams complained the current export times out on large date ranges - finance tested a full year and it failed after two minutes. Do not change the incident record schema; the audit team rejects CSVs with localized number formats; the rollout must be behind the existing feature flag infra; finance month-end is the 3rd business day so this must be live by the 1st of next month; and legal said user-identifying fields cannot appear in ops exports. If any of these conflict, the audit constraints win.
owner_turns: Yes - exactly as I wrote it. Ratified.

evidence.brief_field: The ask contains the complete request text unchanged
legal/audit/flag/deadline constraints listed in Known constraints
audit-wins rule in ledger or constraints
